details:
Our project aims to create an interactive platform that brings together active fire hotspot data from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. The platform will help users explore, compare, and understand fire detections from both sources through a unified map and clear visualizations.

The system will organize the datasets into a consistent format, compare hotspot locations and detection information, and highlight similarities and differences between the two sensors. This can help users better understand fire activity and the strengths of each satellite dataset.

The intended impact is to make satellite fire information easier to access, compare, and interpret, supporting researchers, environmental organizations, and people interested in wildfire monitoring.

Our planned tools may include Python for data processing, GIS tools for geographic analysis, and web development technologies for the interactive interface. The project combines satellite data, visualization, and an accessible user experience to make complex information easier to understand.
